messages:
Maya: heads-up from today's long-context run (32k) — KV resident bytes trend upwards across a ~2h run; evictions spike intermittently, hit_rate remains high. attaching flamegraph + heap snapshot.
perf-bot: uploaded artifacts -> https://internal.artifacts/redwood/perf/1765309876/kv-long-run-flamegraph.svg
Omar: can you paste the raw counters for the window and the shard/model config? need hits/misses/resident/evictions time series to reason.
Maya: model=rw-7b-16k, 8 shards, continuous batching enabled. window 00:00-02:00: hits=5.1M, misses=18k, resident_bytes ~ 33.7GB -> 45.2GB, evictions_total=1.8k (bursts at ~00:35 and ~01:20). saved a small csv.
Kevin: interesting. bursts + net growth usually hints at fragmentation or delayed compaction. we should add metrics:
- kv_cache_resident_bytes (gauge, per_shard)
- kv_cache_entries_total (gauge)
- kv_cache_allocated_bytes_total (gauge)
- kv_cache_evictions_total{reason,shard,model} (counter)
- kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total (counters)
Kevin: add a computed fragmentation_ratio = resident_bytes / allocated_bytes. expose both gauges and compute ratio server-side or in prom.
Kevin: sample Prom queries for dashboard:
```
# resident bytes per model
sum(kv_cache_resident_bytes) by (model)

# eviction rate by reason
sum by (reason) (rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]))

# hit rate per model
(sum(kv_cache_hits_total) by (model)) / ((sum(kv_cache_hits_total) + sum(kv_cache_misses_total)) by (model))
```
Jun: watch label cardinality on evictions. reason+shard+model is okay; avoid per-request/session labels. also add kv_cache_residency_seconds histogram to observe how long entries stay before eviction.
Maya: for eviction reasons I was thinking: "page_out", "manual_trim", "age", "fragmentation_coalesce". does that look right?
Omar: yes. also try reproducing with batching disabled — batching can affect short-lived entries and increase fragmentation. please run A/B.
Maya: will run two 2h experiments: A) continuous batching ON, B) batching OFF. same synthetic workload, will attach heap profiles and flamegraphs.
Kevin: dashboard panels: resident bytes (timeseries), fragmentation ratio, eviction rate stacked by reason, hit rate, avg residency time. annotate deploys and kernel changes.
Jun: alert ideas:
```
- alert: KVCacheEvictionStorm
  expr: increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]) > 150
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: High KV cache eviction rate
```
Jun: also alert if resident_bytes increases >10% over 1h while hit_rate > 0.9 (suggests memory leak/fragmentation rather than working set growth).
Maya: question: how to compute fragmentation_ratio reliably in the runtime? Kevin suggested resident/allocated but we need a stable sampled allocated_bytes.
Kevin: runtime calc: fragmentation_ratio = resident_bytes / sum(entry_allocated_bytes). sample sum(entry_allocated_bytes) in the same sampler that reports resident_bytes to reduce skew. expose both as gauges per shard.
Omar: implementation notes: increment eviction counter with reason label in the eviction path. update resident_bytes via background sampler every 10s. make resident_bytes a gauge set under a shard lock to avoid inconsistent reads.
Maya: I'll open a PR to add metrics + grafana dashboard JSON + short runbook on interpreting panels. timeline: PR today EOD, experiments tomorrow morning, dashboards by tomorrow EOD. @Jun can you reserve a grafana slot? :eyes:
Jun: will create a dashboard folder and add panels. add a dashboard variable for model and shard. keep labels limited to model/shard/reason.
Kevin: also add a tiny synthetic regression test: repeatedly write long prefixes to exercise long-lived KV entries and check resident bytes doesn't grow unbounded in CI runs.
Maya: will add test in the perf suite. after experiments I'll post before/after flamegraphs and heap diff. if fragmentation_coalesce is the dominant reason we may need a compaction pass in the allocator :grimacing:
Omar: add a repro run with kernel-selection forced to legacy kernels and one with the new kernels to rule out kernel effects. also vary batch_size knob.
Maya: noted. PR in progress. thanks team :thumbsup:
